name: Usher Syndrome Type I

criteria.description: Congenital severe to profound sensorineural hearing loss
Progressive retinitis pigmentosa leading to vision loss
Identification of pathogenic variants in USH1 genes (e.g., MYO7A, CDH23)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital severe-profound sensorineural hearing loss, vestibular dysfunction, and clinical or electrophysiological evidence of retinitis pigmentosa
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical criteria are met

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital severe to profound sensorineural hearing loss
Vestibular areflexia with delayed motor milestones
searchTerms: lack of balance reflexes with delayed motor skills
balance reflex absence leading to motor delay

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive retinitis pigmentosa causing night blindness and peripheral vision loss
searchTerms: progressive night blindness and tunnel vision
gradual loss of peripheral and night vision

common.symptomName: Delayed walking age due to vestibular dysfunction
searchTerms: late walking due to balance problems
slow motor milestone because of balance loss

occasional.symptomName: Mild cognitive delay secondary to sensory deprivation
searchTerms: mild learning delay from sensory loss
slight cognitive impairment due to sensory deprivation
mild developmental delay related to sensory issues
abnormal spine shape due to balance loss

rare.symptomName: Speech delay due to hearing impairment
searchTerms: speech delay due to hearing loss

laboratory: Audiometry showing bilateral severe to profound sensorineural hearing loss
imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing retinal pigment epithelium degeneration
Electroretinography (ERG) with reduced or absent rod and cone responses
genetic: Pathogenic variants in USH1 genes such as MYO7A, CDH23, PCDH15, USH1C, and USH1G
other: Delayed motor milestones due to vestibular dysfunction
Fundoscopic evidence of bone-spicule pigmentation in retina

distinguishingFeatures: Moderate to severe hearing loss (not congenital profound)
Isolated hearing loss without retinal or vestibular involvement

redFlags: Delayed walking beyond 18 months due to vestibular dysfunction
Early onset night blindness or peripheral vision loss
references: Smith RJH, et al. Usher Syndrome. GeneReviews. 2020.
Petit C. Usher syndrome: from genetics to pathogenesis. Annu Rev Genomics Hum Genet. 2001.
Jin H, et al. Clinical and genetic characteristics of Usher syndrome type I. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2019.
